cur:monumental-sma-christ-enthroned-fath.summary: Along the left aisle, a long row of standing saints and Fathers of the Western and Eastern Churches converges on the enthroned Christ at the centre, while scenes from the Old Testament stories of Noah and Joseph run in a frieze above. The great wall gathers the whole Church, Latin and Greek, around Christ.
facts: Santa Maria Antiqua in the Roman Forum preserves wall paintings from the 6th to the late 8th century; buried after an earthquake in 847, it was rediscovered only in 1900.
Inscriptions in the church shift from Greek (under Martin I) to Greek and Latin (under John VII) and finally Latin alone (under Paul I), reflecting Rome's changing ties to Byzantium.

cur:monumental-sma-christ-enthroned-fath.notes: The photograph shows the whole wall; Christ is the central enthroned figure.

walters:71.277.summary: Beneath a pointed trefoil arch with a crocketed gable, Christ hangs from the cross crowned with thorns, his head fallen to one side. At the left, the swooning Virgin is held up by the other holy women; at the right stand John, holding a book with his hand on his breast, and a bearded man in a hat. Though coarsely carved and much rubbed, the large leaf conveys the grief of the Passion with clarity.
facts: The Walters describes the group at the left as the Three Marys and the bearded figure at the right as 'a Hebrew', standing beside John.
The leaf, almost 20 cm high, was once hinged to a companion panel; its hinges are lost.
It was in the collection of Raoul Heilbronner (sold in Paris, 1921) before Henry Walters bought it the same year.
walters:71.277.notes: The Walters date label reads '3rd quarter 14th century' but the date fields give 1375–1400; 'second half of the 14th century' covers both. Worklist year 800 was a parsing error.
